objective: Settle the factual open points of the 0.3.0 pi integration plan about Kimi for Coding (global) and Kimi K3.1, from Moonshot's and the extensions' official sources.
scope: Context: /home/user/holyagent/docs/pi/providers.md; the earlier finding that pi-provider-kimi-code (https://github.com/Leechael/pi-provider-kimi-code) layers on pi's built-in kimi-coding provider; the open points list /home/user/holyagent-work/pi-open.md (ids 3.6, 5.11, 5.12, 5.14, 5.15, 5.17, 5.18).

Answer, each with a dated source link: (5.11, 5.17) which pi provider id and which host serve Kimi for Coding for international (global) users, api.kimi.com or api.kimi.ai, and how KIMI_CODE_REGION selects it; (5.12, 5.18) the Kimi for Coding model ids, which ones are Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K2.8 Preview (the maintainer says kimi-for-coding is K2.8 Preview), their context windows, reasoning or thinking levels, image support, and the subscription's pricing or quota model; login (OAuth, API key and its environment variable); (5.14) how prompt caching works on Kimi for Coding and whether pi's kimi adapter or pi-provider-kimi-code keys it (prompt_cache_key) and honors PI_CACHE_RETENTION; (5.15) whether current pi still ships the kimi-coding provider; (3.6) Moonshot's official Kimi K3.1 prompting or instruction guide: its URL, date or version, and a summary of its recommendations on system prompts, tool use, thinking mode, temperature and output length; (5.19) whether pi-provider-kimi-code issue #16 is fixed and what its Moonshot-side tools send to Moonshot.
Use Moonshot's platform and Kimi Code documentation, kimi.com, the Kimi Code CLI repository, pi's sources and the extension's repository. Separate sourced facts from inference.
constraints: Read-only: write no files and make no git writes; the full answer goes in the report.
Keep working until done; stop and report. Report in under 600 words, one short entry per open point id with its answer, source link and date, and 'unknown' where the sources do not say.

result:
result: Kimi for Coding global is host api.kimi.ai; pi's built-in kimi-coding provider is hard-wired to api.kimi.com (mainland), so global needs the extension or a base-URL override. Today is 2026-11-07, and the pages I fetched carried no dates unless noted.

**5.11 / 5.17 (provider id and host)**
- Pi provider id is `kimi-coding`, named "Kimi For Coding". Its base URL is `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1` over `openai-completions`, with auth from `KIMI_API_KEY` or OAuth. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/main/packages/ai/src/providers/kimi-coding.ts (main branch, read today). It has no region switch.
- Moonshot's Kimi Code docs name the hosts. China uses `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1` and overseas uses `https://api.kimi.ai/coding/v1` (Anthropic-style: `https://api.kimi.ai/coding/`). Source: https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/models
- `KIMI_CODE_REGION` belongs to pi-provider-kimi-code, not to pi. Values are `mainland-cn` (the default, `api.kimi.com` and `auth.kimi.com`) and `global` (`api.kimi.ai` and `auth.kimi.ai`). A `region` key in `~/.pi/providers/kimi-coding/config.json` or the project's `.pi/providers/kimi-coding/config.json` wins over the env var. `KIMI_CODE_BASE_URL` and `KIMI_CODE_OAUTH_HOST` override both. Source: https://github.com/Leechael/pi-provider-kimi-code/blob/main/docs/ENV.md
- The extension's own README doc table says the same, and that a wrong-side account gets 401.
- Inference: global users set `KIMI_CODE_REGION=global`, or `KIMI_CODE_BASE_URL=https://api.kimi.ai/coding/v1` with the built-in provider.

**5.12 / 5.18 (models, login, quota)**
- Source for all model rows: https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/models (K3.1 Pro rollout; K2.8 Preview rollout 2026-09-11).

| Model id | Version | Context | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k3.1-pro` | K3.1 Pro | 1,048,576 on Pro+/Allegretto+; 262,144 on Plus/Moderato | thinking only |
| `k3.1-pro-highspeed` | K3.1 Pro Highspeed | up to 1,048,576 | about 2-3x speed, about 2x quota; Pro+ only |
| `k3` | K3 | 1M or 256K by tier | |
| `k3-256k` | K3 | 262,144 | |
| `kimi-for-coding` | K2.8 Preview | up to 1,048,576 | the maintainer is right: same id, upgraded in place |
| `kimi-for-coding-highspeed` | K2.7 Code Highspeed | 262,144 | |

- Reasoning is `low`, `high` or `max`. The default is `high` for K3.1 Pro and K3, and `max` for `kimi-for-coding`. K3.1 Pro rejects thinking-off with a 400. The other models route thinking-off requests to K2.8 Preview without thinking. A mistyped model id also falls back to K2.8 Preview without thinking.
- Image and video input is supported on all except `k3-256k`, which takes image only.
- K3.1 Pro is not served under the id `kimi-for-coding`. Its id is `k3.1-pro`. The extension's fallback list (`kimi-for-coding`, `kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, `k3`) omits it; its README says the live catalog `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1/models` is authoritative.
- Quota is a subscription with a 5-hour rolling window plus a monthly quota. Legacy plans also keep a weekly window. High-speed variants burn quota faster, and switching model or effort invalidates the cache. Sources: https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/error-reference.html and https://kimi-ai.free/use-cases/developers/ (third-party, 2026-08-23). Per-plan prices are unknown from official sources. A third-party page lists legacy tiers at RMB 49 / 99 / 199 / 699 per month (https://jia.je/kb/en/software/coding_plan.html).
- Login is OAuth (`/login kimi-coding`, token in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`) or API key in `KIMI_API_KEY`. The extension also reuses the official `kimi-code` CLI credential file. The Moonshot-side tools need OAuth, not the key.

**5.14 (prompt caching)**
- Moonshot's Messages API reference (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/messages) says `metadata.user_id` is used to improve cache hit rate. For coding agents, set it to the session id.
- Moonshot's Chat reference describes `prompt_cache_key` as required to improve hit rate on Kimi Code Plan. This is as quoted by Kimi Code maintainer 7Sageer on 2026-09-07 in https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/issues/3506.
- Measurements in the extension's docs/caching.md (https://github.com/Leechael/pi-provider-kimi-code/blob/main/docs/caching.md) contradict that. Its measurements show Kimi ignores both `prompt_cache_key` and `cache_control`. The cache is a content-prefix hash, aligned to 256-token chunks, with a TTL between 300 s and 1800 s. Cold `pi` runs do not share cache.
- The extension injects `prompt_cache_key` anyway. `PI_CACHE_RETENTION=none` only skips that injection and has no effect on actual caching.
- I found no `prompt_cache_key` handling for kimi-coding in pi's built-in provider. Pi's `promptCacheKeyMode` defaults to `auto`, which sends the key only to api.openai.com. The first sentence is an inference from the provider file and docs; I did not read pi's `openai-completions.ts`. The cache-key conclusion therefore rests on third-party measurement of the extension.
- `PI_CACHE_RETENTION` does not extend Kimi's cache. The 1h TTL option (`prompt_cache_options.ttl`) exists on Moonshot's platform API, and Moonshot's own context-caching guide (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/context-caching) documents it. Whether the Coding endpoint honors it is unknown. The Kimi Code CLI has no setting for it (issue #3942).

**5.15 (does current pi ship kimi-coding)**
- Yes. `kimi-coding` is in `main` (`models.generated.ts` and `providers/kimi-coding.ts`) and in the pi-ai README. It first shipped in pi 0.50.3 (https://pi.dev/changelog/releases/0.50.3). The extension README says built-in provider support is in v0.82.0+, and refers to the built-in as the recommended path.
- I did not read the exact version number you plan to pin, so the pin itself is unknown.

**3.6 (K3.1 prompting guide)**
- There is no K3.1-specific prompting guide. Moonshot's general guide is https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/prompt-best-practice (undated). It covers clear instructions, roles, explicit steps, few-shot examples, length by paragraphs or bullets, reference text, and summarizing long histories.
- The K3.1 Pro quickstart (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/kimi-k3-1-pro-quickstart) and https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-reasoning-effort give these constraints:
  - Thinking is always on. Do not send `thinking`; use top-level `reasoning_effort` instead.
  - `temperature` is fixed at 1.0, `top_p` at 0.95, and `n` at 1. Omit them from requests.
  - `max_completion_tokens` defaults to 131072 and can go up to 1048576.
  - Pass the whole assistant message back unchanged, including `reasoning_content` and `tool_calls`.
  - Vision does not accept public image URLs.
- The agent guide (https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/guide/use-kimi-k3-to-setup-agent) says to keep the system prompt to role, workflow and quality boundaries, and to put argument details in the tool schema.

**5.19 (extension issue #16)**
- Fixed. Issue #16 was closed on 2026-06-18. PR #25 dedups tool schemas with `$ref`/`$defs` to stay under Moonshot's 15 KB per-tool limit, and the fix shipped in extension 0.6.2 (2026-06-19). Source: https://github.com/Leechael/pi-provider-kimi-code/issues/16. The root cause was a pi-subagents schema bug (nicobailon/pi-subagents#235).
- The extension's open-issues count is 0. A related pi-subagents issue (#249) is referenced.
- The Moonshot-side tools are all off by default, and they need OAuth. `moonshot_search` and `moonshot_fetch` send queries and URLs to Moonshot's services. `kimi_datasource` calls Kimi's `/tools` endpoint with a datasource name and params (such as arxiv or SEC EDGAR queries). The exact request payloads are not documented beyond that, so their contents are unknown.
- Moonshot itself says web search is being updated and is not recommended for production workflows for now.
